key_insight: EATS improves medical reasoning agents’ tool selection by retrieving relevant past tool-use experiences rather than relying only on tool descriptions.
clinical_relevance: Experience-guided tool use could support medical image question answering and report generation, though clinical benefit is not established.
method: Store queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback in a memory.
Retrieve relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries.
Expand memory with test-time interactions without ground-truth supervision.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains in tool selection and downstream performance across four public datasets and three multimodal LLMs, but provides no effect sizes.
watch_item: Self-evaluated memories may retain incorrect tool-use patterns, warranting independent validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
